figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 1. Comparison of monomers used in the resin composition to fabricate 3D printed adsorbents, BEMA (a) and BUMA (b) with the monomers utilized to prepared 
Diaion HP-20, copolymer of styrene (c) and divinylbenzene (d). In red are highlighted the vinyl double bonds that react in the presence of radicals during radical 
polymerisation.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 2. Diagram displaying the steps to fabricate 3D printed adsorbents. The process involves CAD designing (a) 3D printing (b) and post processing to finally obtain 
a 3D printed model (c) made of a porous material (d).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 3. (a) Pore size distributions of 3D printed adsorbents investigated in this work. SEM photographs at x5000 of 3D printed gyroid cubes fabricated with (b) 
BEMA30, (c) BEMA40, (d) BEMA60 and (e) BEMAP2.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 4. Adsorption kinetics on the different 3D materials and on Diaion HP-20 for (a) Sudan 1 and (b) paclitaxel. All adsorption kinetics experiments were carried out 
with an initial concentration of Sudan 1 and paclitaxel of 100 ppm. The experimental data was fitted with the PFO (dashed lines), PSO (continuous line) and pore 
diffusion (dotted lines) models. Error bars represent mean standard deviation (n = 3).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 5. Comparison of outer and inner surface of 3D printed materials used in Sudan 1 adsorption. The white or pale orange colour in the inner sections of BEMA30 
and BEMA40 suggested hindered diffusion due to small pore size.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 6. Adsorption isotherms on the 3D printed materials investigated and Diaion HP-20 for Sudan 1 (a) and Paclitaxel (b). Values represent mean standard deviation 
(n = 3).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 7
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 7. Biomass (a) and taxadiene (b) concentration obtained in cultivations with BEMA40, Diaion HP-20 and no adsorbent control at small-scale (5 mL). Error bars 
represent mean standard deviation (n = 3) (**p < 0.01; Tukey´s honest significant difference).
